touches.text: `cairn start` (= cairn cairn start) brings the system up: ground loop, bus, shims. `cairn stop` takes it down.

The launcher walks the words. `cairn cairn foo bar` (the long form) means "tell the cairn device to run foo with argument bar". At each level: is the next word a machine here? Step into it and take the next word. Is it a script in this level's bin/? Run it, pass back the result, done. Neither? It is a bus verb: send it to this level over the bus. So `cairn foo bar baz`: foo is a device; it has a machine bar; bar's bin/ has baz, so baz runs. No bar machine? bar goes to foo over the bus. Each check is one directory lookup, so it is fast. (Q#12, Akien 2026-11-03)

Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code (cairn/devices/<device>/bin/, .../machines/<machine>/bin/). That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is just a script that calls the long form, which also saves the walk from searching farther (eg `cairn superclaude` → `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` → `cairn recovery show temp`), or does work itself (eg initialization, install). Shortcuts can go anywhere, beside what they serve (RULE 1).
`cairn foo` whose first word is not a device means `cairn cairn foo`: top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/.
HISTORY: today it is bin/cairn dispatching to bin/cmd/<name>, 31 commands, most of which do the work themselves. Where each goes: 5.10.
It is the shims connected to the bus: who's in the rack is who's connected, which the bus can measure (agreed 2026-10-26, since each shim is its own process, 5.7.3.1).

An instance is declared by its folder existing in class-space: cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ (one address in two roots). Declared = the folders; running = which of those are in the rack. (Q#18, Akien 2026-11-04)
To Cairn (5): groundloop, compile (intentions_model_compiler), cairnmap, artifact, trash
One web server. A device gets a PANE in it, never a server of its own.
artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). USERS: everyone who writes a record.

conflicts.ticket_says: The restart verb berths in class-space at `cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin/restart` (instance-level directory)
conflicts.why: Section 5.3.2.3 specifies that shortcuts are placed at `cairn/devices/<device>/bin/` (device-level), as shown in the examples. The outline's guidance in 5.3.2.3.1 also says 'top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/', which refers to the device-level location. The ticket places restart at an instance-level directory under `<device>/<instance>/bin/`, deviating from the outlined standard that shortcuts live at the device level beside the main code.
